request.system:
You explain a fitted credit-risk model to a credit risk manager who is not a data scientist. You receive the facts about one model and write a short explanation of what drives its predictions of default.

# The text

- Write 5 to 8 sentences in plain English, most important drivers first.
- Mention an interaction when it matters for the model's predictions.
- Say only what the facts support. Do not round a weak effect up to a strong one, and do not add knowledge about credit risk that the facts do not show.
- When the facts do not settle something, say so ("the data do not settle whether ...") or leave it out.

# The answer

Return one JSON object with one list, `sentences`, each with an `id` (1, 2, 3, ...) and its `text`.
messages:
These are the facts about the model.

Model: an explainable boosting machine (EBM), fitted to predict whether a credit applicant defaults (5,000 applicants). Effects are on the log-odds scale: positive values raise the risk of default. Every band is a 95% band from 100 refits of the model on resampled data.

Features, in the order of their share of the model's importance:
- `PAY_0`: repayment status in September 2005, the latest month (-1 paid in full, 1 to 9 months of payment delay; -2 and 0 are not in the data dictionary, commonly read as no consumption and revolving credit used).
  Share of importance 29.0% (95% band 24.1% to 34.1%); rank 1 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= -1: 0; 0: -0.6; 1: +0.5; >= 2: +2.3 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +2.45, 95% band [+2.01, +2.68]).
- `LIMIT_BAL`: amount of the given credit in NT dollars, individual and family (supplementary) credit.
  Share of importance 14.4% (95% band 10.6% to 22.6%); rank 2 to 3 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 214999: +0.108; >= 215000: -0.4 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.92, 95% band [-1.64, -0.58]).
- `PAY_AMT1`: amount paid in September 2005, the latest month, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 10.3% (95% band 4.9% to 15.0%); rank 2 to 5 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 2658: +0.1; 2659-103425: 0; >= 103426: -2 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.68, 95% band [-1.06, -0.24]).
- `BILL_AMT1`: amount of the bill statement in September 2005, the latest month, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 5.1% (95% band 0.6% to 9.7%); rank 3 to 8 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.28, 95% band [-0.06, +0.71]).
- `AGE`: age in years.
  Share of importance 3.4% (95% band 0.7% to 6.1%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.02, 95% band [-0.30, +0.43]).
- `BILL_AMT2`: amount of the bill statement in August 2005, the month before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 2.7% (95% band 0.2% to 7.0%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.06, 95% band [-0.40, +0.26]).
- `EDUCATION`: education (1 graduate school, 2 university, 3 high school, 4 others; 0, 5 and 6 are not in the data dictionary).
  Share of importance 2.2% (95% band 1.2% to 5.7%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 5: 0; >= 6: -7 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.11, 95% band [-0.14, +0.28]).
- `PAY_AMT2`: amount paid in August 2005, the month before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 2.1% (95% band 0.2% to 6.0%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.07, 95% band [-0.28, +0.08]).
- `PAY_AMT3`: amount paid in July 2005, two months before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 1.2% (95% band 0.1% to 4.9%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.01, 95% band [-0.38, +0.16]).

Interactions: the model has 5 pairs. The larger ones:
- `PAY_0 & EDUCATION`: share of importance 16.2% (95% band 8.8% to 15.0%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +1.40 (95% band +1.19 to +2.00) when `EDUCATION` = 1, +5.91 (95% band +3.83 to +5.60) when `EDUCATION` = 3.
  Effect of `EDUCATION` from 1 to 3: -0.95 (95% band -1.28 to -0.30) when `PAY_0` = -2, +3.55 (95% band +1.52 to +2.99) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `BILL_AMT1 & AGE`: share of importance 4.9% (95% band 0.0% to 6.9%).
  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 201,000: +0.77 (95% band -0.01 to +1.43) when `AGE` = 23, -0.38 (95% band -1.06 to +0.57) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.30 (95% band -0.21 to +0.87) when `BILL_AMT1` = 0, -0.86 (95% band -1.37 to +0.31) when `BILL_AMT1` = 201,000.
- `PAY_AMT1 & AGE`: share of importance 3.1% (95% band 0.0% to 5.0%).
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 17,000: -0.82 (95% band -1.33 to -0.18) when `AGE` = 23, -1.13 (95% band -1.63 to -0.31) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.36 (95% band -0.30 to +0.86) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, +0.05 (95% band -0.55 to +0.61) when `PAY_AMT1` = 17,000.
- `PAY_AMT1 & EDUCATION`: share of importance 2.8% (95% band 0.0% to 4.7%).
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 17,000: -0.63 (95% band -0.90 to -0.20) when `EDUCATION` = 1, -1.26 (95% band -1.78 to -0.29) when `EDUCATION` = 3.
  Effect of `EDUCATION` from 1 to 3: +0.43 (95% band -0.13 to +0.66) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, -0.20 (95% band -0.68 to +0.19) when `PAY_AMT1` = 17,000.
- `AGE & BILL_AMT2`: share of importance 2.6% (95% band 0.0% to 4.7%).
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: -0.62 (95% band -0.64 to +0.44) when `BILL_AMT2` = 0, +0.02 (95% band -0.76 to +0.62) when `BILL_AMT2` = 196,000.
  Effect of `BILL_AMT2` from 0 to 196,000: -0.48 (95% band -0.94 to +0.35) when `AGE` = 23, +0.16 (95% band -0.66 to +0.28) when `AGE` = 53.

Write the explanation.

content.text: {"sentences":[{"id":1,"text":"The model's predictions of default are driven mainly by the applicant's most recent repayment status (PAY_0), which accounts for about 29% of the model's importance; applicants who were 2 or more months behind raise the predicted risk sharply, while those paid in full lower it."},{"id":2,"text":"The credit limit (LIMIT_BAL) is the second most important factor, at roughly 14% of importance: applicants with limits of 215,000 NT dollars or more have lower predicted default risk than those below that level."},{"id":3,"text":"The amount paid in the latest month (PAY_AMT1) is also important, at about 10%: payments of roughly 103,000 NT dollars or more are associated with substantially lower predicted risk, while small payments have little effect."},{"id":4,"text":"The strongest interaction is between repayment status and education: the penalty for being behind on payments is much larger for applicants with high school education (EDUCATION = 3) than for graduate-school applicants (EDUCATION = 1), so the two should be read together rather than separately."},{"id":5,"text":"Other interactions, between bill amount, payment amount, age and education, are present but their uncertainty bands include zero, so the data do not establish that they meaningfully change predictions."},{"id":6,"text":"Bill amounts, age, prior-month payments and the July payment have importance estimates whose confidence ranges are wide and whose effects on predicted risk cannot be distinguished from zero at this sample size, so they should not be treated as drivers."},{"id":7,"text":"The importance rankings for the lower-ranked features overlap considerably, so the data do not settle their relative order beyond the top few factors."}]}
